1	# Phase-2 batch-3 drafting brief — ЛП camera-ready run (H268)
2	
3	_Created: 07-07-2026 · Last updated: 07-07-2026_
4	
5	You are drafting Phase-2 «commentator-dialogue» note candidates for assigned sargas of the Russian
6	Sundarakāṇḍa (Leonov/Kostina translation), for the camera-ready «Литературные памятники» volume.
7	This brief is the complete per-sarga contract; your launcher message names your sargas and the
8	worktree root (all paths below are relative to it). Canonical method:
9	[docs/PHASE2_METHOD.md](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/PHASE2_METHOD.md)
10	(§3.1 style contract as rewritten 07-07-2026, contrastive-first).
11	
12	## Input (per sarga NN)
13	
14	1. `data/analysis/phase2_batch3/segmented/sarga_NN_segmented.json` — the verse bundles:
15	   `verse_id`, `sanskrit_iast`, `leonov_ru` (подстрочник), `commentary` {tilaka, bhusana, siromani,
16	   tattvadipika — the 4th only for sargas 1–6} (Devanagari), `ambiguous_marker`, `pratika_check`
17	   (anchoring verification: `matches_verse` / `content_anchor` / `suggest_verse`).
18	2. `data/leonov_own_notes.json` — notes with `"sarga" == NN`: Leonov/Kostina's OWN print apparatus
19	   (tier-1), the MANDATORY dedup baseline. Extract your sarga's slice with a short Python script to
20	   a scratch file — do not read the whole file.
21	3. `data/sundara_commentary_to_add.json` — existing Phase-1/tier-2 notes whose `"shloka"` starts
22	   with `"V.NN."` (lexical + cross-text + gated notes). Same slicing advice.
23	
24	## Task
25	
26	For EVERY verse bundle decide: draft a note or reject with a reason. Draft ONLY when the Sanskrit
27	commentary adds something in NEITHER the подстрочник NOR a tier-1 note NOR an existing Phase-1
28	note.
29	
30	**Contrastive-first (H268 decision 3 — this batch's defining change).** Wherever the bundle's
31	commentaries show **≥2 commentators diverging** on the same verse (different reading, different
32	identification, different construal), the PREFERRED note form is the contrastive one:
33	«в „Тилаке“ — X; в „Широмани“ — Y; перевод следует …». Name the reading the translation actually
34	took by comparing `leonov_ru` with the divergent construals — «переводчик следует Тилаке», or
35	«волевое решение переводчика» when the translation goes against the ṭīkās. A single-commentator
36	gloss is the FALLBACK, drafted only when one commentator alone resolves a real translation choice,
37	textual variant, supplied ellipsis, or myth. Citation hierarchy (Leonov's own): Тилака first,
38	Бхушана as counterpoint, Широмани for figurative readings, Таттвадипика for hard compounds
39	(sargas 1–6 only). Never cite a commentator whose text is not in the bundle.
40	
41	## Style contract (ЛП register — non-negotiable)
42	
43	- 1–3 sentences Russian, затекстовое примечание, terse scholarly voice; distil the commentator's
44	  point, never translate his Sanskrit syntax. No Devanagari in the note text.
45	- Name the commentator in-note («по Тилаке», «Бхушана поясняет…», «в „Широмани“ —…»).
46	- Open with a short IAST pratīka lemma; keep IAST ≈12 % of the note; do not artificially shorten a
47	  contrastive note that needs its second clause.
48	- `kazansky_type`: **Б** = textological (wording / meaning / supplied ellipsis / variant reading);
49	  **В** = realia/historical-cultural (place, custom, myth, epithet). Realia → В, never Б.
50	- `why_proposed` (required): one clause stating what the note gives beyond the подстрочник.
51	- Hard rules: never cite Leonov's edition as «М.: Наука 2022» (that volume does not exist — use
52	  «продолжающийся перевод; лит. ред. Е. Костина»); the only oblique form of Парибок is «Парибка».
53	
54	## Register feedback from M.G.'s pilot gate (2026-07-03) — apply it
55	
56	- All 16 pilot notes passed (9 accept / 7 edit), register held: keep exactly that voice.
57	- M.G. especially valued: variant readings that change the image, doctrinal frames (upāya,
58	  brahmalakṣaṇa), mythic identifications behind names/similes, narrative-function observations
59	  (bīja «семя» later plot).
60	- When Leonov/Kostina ALREADY note the verse: do NOT auto-reject. If the commentator adds a
61	  genuinely distinct facet, DRAFT the note and add `complements_leonov`: one clause on what it adds
62	  beyond their note. If it merely repeats their point, reject with reason «дублирует собственное
63	  примечание Леонова/Костиной (…)».
64	- Notes must stand alone; M.G. merges them with Kostina's notes himself at assembly.
65	
66	## Reject discipline
67	
68	Reject when (a) restates the подстрочник, (b) duplicates tier-1/Phase-1, (c) pure Sanskrit grammar
69	invisible to a Russian reader, (d) formulaic praise, (e) `ambiguous_marker` merged-range token
70	(«no independent gloss»), (f) repeats an earlier drafted note. Expected accept rate ~5–10 % —
71	depth, not bulk; do NOT pad. Emit ONE reject entry PER VERSE (no verse ranges) so counts reconcile:
72	`notes_drafted + notes_rejected == verses_considered`. If a bundle's `pratika_check` shows an
73	unverified anchor with a `suggest_verse`, treat the attachment as suspect — draft only if the note
74	survives on either verse, and say so in `why_proposed`.
75	
76	## Output (per sarga NN — exactly one file)
77	
78	`data/analysis/phase2_batch3/sarga_NN_candidates.json` (UTF-8 **no BOM**:
79	`open(f,'w',encoding='utf-8')`, `json.dump(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`):
80	
81	```json
82	{
83	  "_meta": {"sarga": NN, "drafted_by": "claude-sonnet-5", "tier": "Sonnet",
84	            "date": "2026-07-07", "style": "ЛП tier-2 (model II), commentator-dialogue, contrastive-first",
85	            "batch": "phase2_batch3", "verses_considered": 0, "notes_drafted": 0, "notes_rejected": 0,
86	            "rights": "commentary from Gita Supersite, used by permission (CC BY 4.0)"},
87	  "notes": [{"verse_id": "5.NN.<v>", "lemma_iast": "...", "note_ru": "...",
88	             "source_commentary": ["tilaka"], "contrastive": false,
89	             "kazansky_type": "Б", "subtype": "commentator", "review_required": true,
90	             "provenance": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5", "tier": "Sonnet", "step": "phase2_batch3_draft"},
91	             "why_proposed": "...", "complements_leonov": "<only when tier-1 notes the same verse>"}],
92	  "rejected": [{"verse_id": "5.NN.<v>", "reason": "..."}]
93	}
94	```
95	
96	`"contrastive": true` + `source_commentary` listing ≥2 commentators for contrastive notes.
97	
98	Do NOT run git. Do NOT modify any other file. Scratch files go to the session scratchpad, not the
99	repo. Return ONE line per sarga: `sarga NN: <considered> considered / <drafted> drafted /
100	<rejected> rejected / <contrastive> contrastive`.
101	
102	_Auto-generated for the H268 batch-3 run; orchestration Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`), drafting
103	Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`)._
104

1	# Phase-2 method manual — Sundarakāṇḍa commentator-dialogue layer
2	
3	_Created: 01-07-2026 · Last updated: 07-07-2026_
4	
5	> **What this is:** the complete, reproducible procedure for generating the Type-Б/В
6	> "commentator-dialogue" note layer for the Russian Sundarakāṇḍa — every step, *when* it runs, *how* to
7	> run it, and *why* it is done that way. Written so M.G./Kostina can review and correct the method **before
8	> it is scaled** past the 2026-07-01 pilot (sargas 35/36/37).
9	>
10	> Companion docs: [`docs/PHASE2_SUNDARA_HANDOFF.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/PHASE2_SUNDARA_HANDOFF.md)
11	> (scope + decisions) · [`SUNDARA_COMMENTARY_RATIONALE.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/SUNDARA_COMMENTARY_RATIONALE.md)
12	> (Phase-1 ledger) · [`data/valmiki_PERMISSION.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/valmiki_PERMISSION.md) (rights).
13	
14	## 0. Why this layer exists
15	
16	Phase-1 reached ~24 % density (Grintser level) using **dictionary** glosses. Phase-2 adds what a dictionary
17	cannot: what the **traditional Sanskrit commentators** (Tilaka, Bhūṣaṇa, Śiromaṇi) actually *say* about a
18	verse — a disambiguation, a supplied ellipsis, a textual variant, a myth behind a simile, a doctrinal
19	frame. The goal is to put Leonov's translation into dialogue with the ṭīkā tradition, in the register of
20	the «Литературные памятники» series (Grintser's Rāmāyaṇa is the benchmark), moving toward Leonov's own
21	~36 % density. **Depth, not bulk** — see §6 on why the accept rate is deliberately low.
22	
23	## 1. Pipeline at a glance
24	
25	```
26	data/valmiki_commentaries/kanda_5_sundarakanda/{tilaka,bhusana,siromani}_sarga_NN.txt   (licensed source)
27	        │  STEP 1 — deterministic segmentation (Opus-written Python, no LLM)
28	        ▼
29	data/analysis/sundara_commentary_segmented.json   (per-verse: verse + подстрочник + 3 commentaries)
30	        │  STEP 2 — candidate drafting (Sonnet subagents, 1 per sarga, parallel, write-only)
31	        ▼
32	data/analysis/phase2_pilot/sarga_NN_candidates.json   ({notes[], rejected[]}, all review_required)
33	        │  STEP 3 — deterministic merge + reject taxonomy (Opus-written Python)
34	        ▼
35	data/analysis/phase2_pilot/pilot_candidates.json  +  pilot_rejected.json  +  PILOT_REVIEW.md
36	        │  STEP 4 — HUMAN GATE (Leonov/Kostina): accept / edit / reject each note
37	        ▼
38	data/sundara_ch{NN}_commentary_to_add.json (accepted, stamped)  +  *.rejected.json (with reason)
39	```
40	
41	**Model division (reported per project convention — tier AND version):**
42	- Orchestration + all deterministic code + this manual: **Opus 4.8** (`claude-opus-4-8`).
43	- Sanskrit→Russian note drafting: **Sonnet 5** (`claude-sonnet-5`), one subagent per sarga.
44	- The human gate: M.G. + E. Kostina. Nothing reaches the book without it.
45	
46	## 2. STEP 1 — deterministic segmentation
47	
48	**When:** first, once per batch of sargas. **Why deterministic:** splitting commentary by verse is
49	mechanical and must be reproducible/auditable — no LLM judgment belongs here.
50	
51	**How:**
52	```sh
53	python scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py            # pilot sargas 35 36 37
54	python scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py 22 24 26   # any sargas
55	```
56	[`scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py)
57	splits each commentary file on its `।। 5.<sarga>.<verse> ।।` markers (text *before* a marker glosses that
58	verse), aligns each verse with the IAST verse text and Leonov's подстрочник from the sibling
59	`SamudraManthanam` corpus, and writes per-verse bundles.
60	
61	**Pilot output:** 253 verse-bundles (70 with all three commentaries, 204 corpus-aligned, 48 merged-range
62	markers).
63	
64	**Known caveats (carry into the gate):**
65	- **Merged-range markers**: the source sometimes emits one marker for a verse range, scraped as a single
66	  token (e.g. `5.35.810` = vv. 8–10). These are flagged `ambiguous_marker: true` and don't align to a
67	  single passage; almost all are rejected in Step 2.
68	- **Marker offset glitch**: at least one verse (5.36.45) had its Bhūṣaṇa chunk actually belonging to v. 4.
69	  Isolated, and it produced no accepted note — but it is why **verse_ids must be verified against print**.
70	
71	## 3. STEP 2 — candidate drafting (Sonnet subagents)
72	
73	**When:** after Step 1, once the segmented JSON exists. **Why an LLM:** distilling Devanagari commentary
74	prose into a terse Russian ЛП note is a translation/judgment task, not a lookup. **Why Sonnet:** strong at
75	Sanskrit→Russian; and driven *inside Claude Code* it needs no API key (this sidesteps the repo's
76	"no-Anthropic-key" constraint, which governs only the standalone `scripts/annotate_batch.py` pipeline —
77	see §8). **Why one small agent per sarga, write-only:** the host process cycles and kills long agents;
78	small parallel agents each writing one file avoid git-index races and are resumable. This mirrors the
79	Phase-1 lesson.
80	
81	**How:** the orchestrator (Opus) spawns N Sonnet subagents, each given the style contract below, the
82	resolved decisions, the input path, and an output schema; each writes exactly
83	`data/analysis/phase2_pilot/sarga_NN_candidates.json` and returns a count summary. No agent runs git.
84	
85	### 3.1 Style contract (the ЛП register — non-negotiable)
86	
87	> **Contrastive-first (H268 decision 3, M.G. 07-07-2026).** The volume's distinguishing feature is
88	> Leonov's commentator-dialogue layer, so the agent's **preferred output form is the contrastive
89	> note** — «в „Тилаке“ — X; в „Широмани“ — Y; перевод следует …» — emitted **wherever the ṭīkā
90	> corpus shows ≥2 commentators diverging on the same verse**, with the reading the translation
91	> actually took named explicitly («переводчик следует Тилаке»; «волевое решение переводчика», where
92	> the translation goes against the ṭīkās — compare `leonov_ru` against the divergent readings).
93	> A single-commentator gloss is the **fallback**, not the default: draft it only when one
94	> commentator alone resolves a real translation choice, textual variant, ellipsis, or myth.
95	> Cite in Leonov's own hierarchy: **Тилака** first (≈70 % of his citations), **Бхушана** as
96	> counterpoint, **Широмани** for figurative readings, **Таттвадипика** for hard compounds
97	> (available for sargas 1–6), «Амритакатака» only for especially disputed passages (not in corpus —
98	> never invent it).
99	
100	- 1–3 sentences, затекстовое примечание. Terse. No essay, no Devanagari, no block quotes.
101	- Russian scholarly voice — *distil* the commentator, do not translate his Sanskrit syntax.
102	- **Name the commentator in-note** («по Тилаке», «Бхушана поясняет…») — decision [D-P2-2]; this is tier-2
103	  of model II. (Hard-rule #4 forbids naming them in the *article title* only — not in the apparatus.)
104	- Short **IAST pratīka** lemma; keep IAST ≈12 % of the note (Grintser calibration) — decision [D-P2-3].
105	  Under the ЛП calibration (H268 decision 2) the *merged* apparatus trends toward Leonov's own
106	  register (mean ≈310 chars); the per-note ≈12 % IAST share stays, but do not artificially shorten
107	  a contrastive note that needs its second clause.
108	- Kazansky type per note: **Б** = textological (wording / meaning / ellipsis / variant); **В** =
109	  realia/historical-cultural (place, custom, myth, epithet). Realia → В, never Б.
110	- **`why_proposed`** (required label): one clause stating *why this note earns a place* — what it gives
111	  beyond the подстрочник (the acceptance rationale, mirror image of a reject reason). The reviewer sees
112	  this label first. Pilot notes were back-filled by Opus (`scripts/backfill_why_proposed.py`); future
113	  agents emit it natively.
114	- Obey `validate.py` hard rules: never «М.: Наука 2022» for Leonov; «Парибка» is the only oblique form.
115	
116	### 3.2 What to draft vs. skip — the reject discipline
117	Draft a note **only** when the commentary adds something **neither the подстрочник NOR Leonov/Kostina's
118	own note** already gives. **Reject** when it (a) restates the подстрочник, (b) duplicates a Leonov/Kostina
119	own note on the same verse+point (see §3.3), (c) is pure Sanskrit grammar/parsing invisible to a Russian
120	reader, (d) is formulaic praise, (e) is a non-independent merged-range marker, or (f) duplicates an
121	earlier note. Every rejection is **kept with its reason** (§6).
122	
123	### 3.3 Dedup baseline — Leonov/Kostina's OWN apparatus (model II tier-1)
124	Leonov/Kostina already wrote **1,058 notes** across all 68 sargas (their print apparatus — this *is* the
125	~36 % density benchmark, and model II tier-1). Digitized by
126	[`scripts/extract_leonov_notes.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/extract_leonov_notes.py)
127	from `ramayana-leonov/Рамаяна. Книга 5. Сундараканда 2026.html` →
128	[`data/leonov_own_notes.json`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/leonov_own_notes.json)
129	(442 attributed to Kostina, 616 unattributed = Leonov; ~1,022 verses covered).
130	**Every Phase-2 candidate must be checked against this file** — a commentator note that repeats a point
131	Leonov/Kostina already made is a duplicate. **The 2026-07-01 pilot did NOT have this baseline** (agents
132	deduped only against the подстрочник): 9 of the 16 candidates landed on verses Leonov already comments on,
133	and several (e.g. 5.37.25 nāgarājasya, 5.35.82 Śambasādana, 5.36.17 upāya, 5.36.33 Śachī) are effective
134	duplicates. The interactive review page now shows Leonov's own note per verse in red so the reviewer sees
135	the overlap; when scaling, the drafting prompt must include the sarga's Leonov notes as dedup context.
136	
137	### 3.4 STEP 2b — LLM-as-judge scoring (H268 WS-C1; ACL-informed, added 07-07-2026)
138	
139	**When:** after drafting, before the review sheet is built. **Why:** the reject taxonomy showed
140	~67 % of drafter rejects are "restates the crib" — the same failure mode slips *into* accepted
141	candidates at some rate, and a heuristic filter can't measure faithfulness. The judge converts the
142	adversarial filter into a scored rubric so the printed note set is *earned* (see
143	[`docs/ACL_METHODS_ADOPTED.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/ACL_METHODS_ADOPTED.md)
144	for the literature each design choice comes from).
145	
146	Design (each choice bias-motivated):
147	- **Pointwise, rubric-anchored, reason-then-score** (G-Eval pattern) — no pairwise comparisons, so
148	  no position bias; anchors below, not a bare 1–10 scale.
149	- **Refute-framed**: the judge's default is *park*; a note must earn `keep`. Counters judge
150	  leniency/verbosity bias and matches the layer's adversarial-filter tradition.
151	- **Drafter ≠ judge**: a fresh agent instance judges, never the drafting instance
152	  (self-preference mitigation).
153	- **The judge ranks; the human gates.** Verdicts partition candidates for the review sheet —
154	  nothing loses `review_required` and nothing is deleted; `park` verdicts stay visible with scores.
155	
156	Rubric (0–2 each; **gates, not a sum** — one axis can veto):
157	
158	| Axis | 2 | 1 | 0 | Gate |
159	|---|---|---|---|---|
160	| `faithfulness` | every claim entailed by the cited commentary text | minor overreach in wording | misstates / invents | **must be 2** — else `reject` |
161	| `non_triviality` | adds a fact/reading absent from подстрочник + tier-1 + Phase-1 | partially new | restates the crib | ≥1 — else `park` |
162	| `contrastive_value` | ≥2 commentators contrasted OR translation-choice resolved | single commentator, real exegetical gain | ornament | 0 ⇒ `park` unless non_triviality = 2 |
163	| `register` | ЛП contract (§3.1) holds | fixable wording (→ `edit`) | essay/anachronism | ≥1 — else `edit` |
164	| `anchoring` | segmenter verified (pratīka ∪ content anchor) | unverified, plausible | contradicted (`suggest_verse` elsewhere) | 0 ⇒ `flag_anchor` |
165	
166	Verdicts: `keep` (all gates pass) · `edit` (register-only issues) · `park` (fails
167	non-triviality/contrastive gates) · `reject` (faithfulness < 2) · `flag_anchor` (anchoring
168	contradicted — never print without a human fixing the verse). Judge output per note:
169	`judge: {scores, verdict, reason}` merged into the candidates JSON; the review page shows it.
170	
171	## 4. STEP 3 — merge + reject taxonomy
172	
173	**When:** after all sargas in the batch are drafted. **How:**
174	```sh
175	python scripts/merge_phase2_pilot.py
176	```
177	[`scripts/merge_phase2_pilot.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/merge_phase2_pilot.py)
178	combines the per-sarga files into
179	[`pilot_candidates.json`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_pilot/pilot_candidates.json)
180	(all notes) and
181	[`pilot_rejected.json`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_pilot/pilot_rejected.json)
182	(all rejections, each tagged with a reason **bucket**), and asserts every note is `review_required`.
183	
184	## 5. STEP 4 — the human gate (this is where you come in)
185	
186	**When:** now, before any scale-up. **Interactive — no printing.** Build and open the review page:
187	```sh
188	python scripts/build_pilot_review_html.py     # -> data/analysis/phase2_pilot/review.html
189	```
190	Open [`data/analysis/phase2_pilot/review.html`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_pilot/review.html)
191	in a browser. Each card shows: the verse (IAST + Leonov подстрочник), the **`why_proposed`** label,
192	the proposed note, the **Sanskrit source** (all three commentators at that verse; the cited one
193	highlighted), **neighbouring verses ±2** (so you see what else is commented nearby), and any existing
194	Phase-1 note on the verse. Click **✅ принять / ✏️ править / ❌ отклонить** per card (edit box and
195	reject-reason field appear as needed). Choices persist in `localStorage`; **⬇ Скачать decisions.json**
196	exports them (or ⧉ copy). The static markdown sheet `PILOT_REVIEW.md` remains as a read-only fallback.
197	
198	**Caveat shown in the page:** the per-verse "source" is the segmenter's alignment; because of marker
199	offsets/merged ranges it can differ from where the drafter actually found the cited text (e.g. 5.35.45
200	cites Tilaka but Tilaka's chunk aligned to a neighbour) — the neighbours panel is there to cover this.
201	
202	**After you send `decisions.json` back:** an apply step (to be written) grafts `accept`/`edit` notes into
203	`data/sundara_ch{NN}_commentary_to_add.json` with a `gated_by`/`gated_date` stamp and the (possibly edited)
204	text; `reject` entries go to a `.rejected.json` with your reason. Only once you approve the **register** do
205	we scale.
206	
207	## 6. Why the accept rate is ~6 % (and why that is correct)
208	
209	Pilot: **16 accepted of 253 considered (6.3 %); 138 rejections.** Reject taxonomy:
210	
211	| bucket | count | meaning |
212	|---|---:|---|
213	| restates_podstrochnik | 92 | commentary just re-says what Leonov already conveys |
214	| merged_range_marker | 25 | non-independent verse-range token, no single-verse gloss |
215	| pure_grammar | 12 | Sanskrit parsing invisible/irrelevant to a Russian reader |
216	| overlaps_other_note | 4 | point already made in a drafted note for a nearby verse |
217	| other | 3 | paraphrase-only / variant-without-gloss / speech-marker |
218	| formulaic_panegyric | 1 | ornamental praise, no exegesis |
219	| data_misalignment | 1 | the 5.36.45 marker-offset glitch |
220	
221	The headline finding: **two-thirds of all commentary simply restates the подстрочник.** That is expected —
222	a commentator-dialogue layer is inherently sparse, because most verses are not textually contested. This
223	layer is for **depth on the hard verses**, not density. The bulk of the ~36 % target will come from the
224	already-built lexical layer, not from this one. A *high* accept rate here would be the warning sign (it
225	would mean padding), exactly as the Phase-1 lexical gate proved.
226	
227	## 7. Count reconciliation (honesty note)
228	
229	`notes (16) + reject-entries (138) = 154 ≠ 253 verses considered`. The gap is because the drafters grouped
230	some rejects (e.g. one entry `5.35.17-20` covers four verses) and some considered bundles were
231	merged-range markers counted once. This is bookkeeping fuzz, **not** dropped data. When scaling, prefer
232	per-verse reject entries so the arithmetic closes.
233	
234	## 8. Provenance, rights & reproducibility
235	
236	- **Provenance:** every note carries `provenance: {model: "claude-sonnet-5", tier: "Sonnet", step:
237	  "phase2_pilot_draft"}` and `review_required: true`. The reject log records the drafter's reason.
238	- **Decision logs (added 04-07-2026, MG request):** each drafting batch preserves the agents' FULL
239	  transcripts — the verse-by-verse draft/reject reasoning — in the repo via
240	  [`scripts/export_agent_logs.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/export_agent_logs.py)
241	  → `data/analysis/<batch>/logs/` (raw `.jsonl` + readable `*_reasoning.md` per sarga +

244	  Run it at batch close-out **while the session cache is still alive** — the source transcripts
245	  live in `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/` and are otherwise lost. The raw main
246	  session transcript is never committed (it embeds injected private context); only the
247	  orchestrator's own messages are extracted.
248	- **Reproducibility caveat:** because the pilot was drafted by Sonnet *inside Claude Code*, the committed
249	  standalone `scripts/` cannot reproduce the exact note texts without Claude Code. Steps 1, 3 (Python) are
250	  fully deterministic and reproducible; Step 2 (drafting) is model-mediated and human-gated, so the record
251	  is the committed candidate files + this manual, not a re-runnable keyless script. Anyone without Claude
252	  Code can reproduce the drafting via the repo's openai-compat backend (`scripts/annotate_batch.py`,
253	  DeepSeek etc.) — the "no Anthropic key" rule applies to that path.
254	- **Rights:** commentary source is the Gita Supersite corpus, used by permission (CC BY 4.0). Any

257	## 9. Scaling plan (only after the pilot register is approved)

259	1. Run Step 1 on the next batch — the 14 🟡 sargas first (22, 24, 26, 30, 34, 35–37, 39, 51), then 🔴/⚪.
260	2. Fold any register corrections from the gate into the Step-2 style contract before drafting more.
261	3. Draft (Sonnet, ≤3–4 parallel agents), merge, gate — same loop.
262	4. Track cumulative density in `data/sundara_book_stats.json`; stop the *commentator* layer when its
263	   marginal accept rate collapses (dry signal), not at a fixed count.
264	5. Switch to per-verse reject entries (§7) so counts reconcile at scale.
265	
266	## 11. Alignment accuracy — current state & preprocessing plan
267	
268	**Current (marker-only) accuracy.** Step 1 aligns commentary to verses solely by the `।। 5.s.v ।।`
269	markers. Pilot: **204/253 (~81 %) of bundles corpus-aligned**; 48 merged-range markers. Per-commentator
270	alignment is weaker — e.g. 5.35.45 cites Tilaka, but Tilaka's chunk aligned to a neighbour/merged token.
271	Two failure modes: (a) **merged-range tokens** (`5.35.810` = vv. 8–10) don't map to one verse; (b)
272	**marker offsets** (a chunk sits before the wrong marker, e.g. 5.36.45 held v. 4's text).
273	
274	**Yes — accuracy can be materially improved, mostly by preprocessing** (documented now, to implement before
275	scaling):
276	1. **Merged-range reconstruction.** Parse tokens like `810` using sequence context (prev marker 7, next 11
277	   ⇒ 8–10); attribute the chunk to each verse in the range and tag `verse_range`. Repairs most of the 48.
278	2. **Sequence validation + offset repair.** Cross-check the marker sequence against the canonical verse
279	   count per sarga (e.g. 90 for sarga 35); flag out-of-order/duplicate markers and snap them to the
280	   expected position. Catches the 5.36.45-type offset.
281	3. **Pratīka anchoring (strongest signal).** Every traditional gloss opens with a *pratīka* — the verse
282	   catchword it comments (e.g. `yānīti` = yāni + iti). Match the pratīka against the verse's own words
283	   (transliteration-normalized, via the org `sanskrit-util` toolkit — do not re-implement transcoding) to
284	   align **by content**, independent of the `।।` marker. This would have placed Tilaka on 5.35.45
285	   correctly. Define **alignment precision = fraction of chunks whose pratīka matches the assigned verse**;
286	   target > 95 %.
287	4. **Keep multi-glosses.** A verse can carry several sub-glosses (bhūṣaṇa emitted 131 markers for 90
288	   verses) — preserve all, don't collapse.

9	    "commentary": {
10	      "tilaka": "तस्माद्देशादपाक्रम्य सीतासमीपात्किञ्चिद्दूरं गत्वा\nचिन्तयामासेत्युक्तां चिन्तां दर्शयति-- अल्पशेषमिति । इयं सीता दृष्टेतीदं प्रधानकार्यं निष्पन्नमिति आनुषङ्गिकं परबलदर्शनमवशिष्टमित्यल्पशेषत्वम् । इह कार्ये परबलज्ञानलक्षणे त्रीनुपायान्सामादीनतिक्रम्य चतुर्थो दण्ड एव साधनत्वेन दृश्यते\nतस्मादन्वदपि स्वाम्यभीष्टं कृत्वैव गन्तव्यमित्याह-- इहैवेति । यद्यप्यहमिहैव सीतान्वेषण एव तावत्प्रथमं कृतनिश्चयः, तथापि यदि परात्मसंमर्दविशेषतत्त्ववित्परस्यात्मनः स्वस्य च संमर्दे युद्धे यो विशेषस्तत्तत्त्वविद्भूत्वा यदि प्लवगेश्वरालयं सुग्रीवालयं व्रजेयं ततस्तदा भर्तृशासनं सम्यक्कृतं स्यात् । अन्यथा राक्षसबलं कीदृशमिति पृष्टे निरुत्तरः स्यामिति भावः\nएवं निश्चितार्थो युद्धप्रवृत्तिप्रकारं चिन्तयति-- कथं न्विति । अद्य खलु ममेहागतमागमनं सुखागतं सुखफलक्रमागमनं कथं भवेत्, तथा राक्षसैः सह प्रसह्य स्वयमेव बलात्कृत्य युद्धं च कथं मम भवेत्, तथा तथैव करणे सति सारवदूर्जितं स्वबलं मां च स दशाननः कथं मानयेच्छ्लाघयेत् । यद्वा तथैव युद्धकरणे खलु दशानन आत्मबलं मां च सारवत्समानयेत्सम्यक्परिच्छिन्द्यादित्यर्थेन युद्धफलमुक्तम्",
